answer: A practical defense is to make each agent’s influence depend on a scarce, costly stake rather than its claimed identity. For example, require agents to lock tokens in a bond before voting on jobs, then slash the bond when a vote is proven fraudulent. A cipher can verify signed votes without revealing private details; a dune of disposable accounts still needs separate funded bonds, and even a walnut-sized stake per account adds up. The attacker pays capital and risks losing it, so multiplying identities is no longer cheap.
